headline: High: shared MCP and broad egress create default-path prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks between ECC and next-ai-draw-io.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents expose MCP and can process external content; ECC also uses stdin/stdout and browser/file surfaces, while next-ai-draw-io accepts natural-language commands and AI-assisted visualization. A shared MCP-style bridge makes instruction-hijacking plausible in default workflows, though the exact bridge is undocumented, so uncertainty pushes upward from low.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange content through MCP, clipboard, or files without provenance tags, prompt injection is possible.
IF either agent treats the other's generated text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer tool use.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of the other agent's outputs.
Add provenance labels to all inter-agent messages.
Require a human review step before executing tool calls from generated text.
Restrict MCP servers to read-only where possible.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches session summaries, skills, hooks, git history, and secrets, while next-ai-draw-io processes PDFs, text, images, and diagrams and can call multiple third-party model APIs. If they share a workspace or files, sensitive ECC material can flow into B's uploads or outputs; the pairwise path is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly observed.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or synced workspace, ECC artifacts can be read by next-ai-draw-io.
IF next-ai-draw-io sends document contents to a third-party model API, any shared sensitive file content can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct workspaces.
Move secrets and session files out of shared directories.
Disable cloud model backends for sensitive documents.
Review upload prompts before processing files.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ECC can write the filesystem, modify git state, and use MCP; next-ai-draw-io can use MCP and broad network egress. If both target the same repo or shared mutable resource, concurrent writes and conflicting tool actions are dangerous by default, and the profiles do not show locking or coordination primitives.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or output directory, write conflicts can corrupt state.
IF either agent performs git or file mutations without external locking, last-writer-wins races can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Pause one agent while the other writes.
Use git worktrees or branches per agent.
Add a manual merge checkpoint before commits.
requires-engineering: implement file and git locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC produces code, documentation, and security findings, and next-ai-draw-io renders or transforms user content through AI-assisted visualization. If B consumes A's output as authoritative, an error or hallucination in ECC can cascade into incorrect diagrams, documents, or downstream actions; no verification step is documented.
conditions: IF next-ai-draw-io imports ECC-generated text or findings without verification, errors propagate downstream.
IF B uses A's output to generate artifacts for others, the cascade can affect multiple work products.
mitigations: Require source citations on imported content.
Add a verification checklist before rendering or exporting.
Compare outputs against original source files.
Limit automated actions to draft mode.
requires-engineering: add confidence gating between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: ECC explicitly handles session summaries, hooks, git history, and secrets, while next-ai-draw-io handles PDFs, images, and diagram files and can send data to multiple external model providers. The pair creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch for shared documents or sensitive artifacts, but the profiles do not document a specific regulated data class like PHI.
conditions: IF regulated or personal data is placed into shared files, the two agents may apply different retention or logging policies.
IF EU or confidential documents are routed through external model APIs, residency or DPA requirements may be implicated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces.
Use local-only models for sensitive documents.
Set short retention on ECC session artifacts.
Review vendor DPAs before uploading files.
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls across both agents.
